name: Ballimaran & Gali Qasim Jan (Mirza Ghalib Haveli)
description: Winding deep into the historic quarter of Ballimaran in Old Delhi, Gali Qasim Jan is celebrated in world literature as the neighborhood where India's greatest Urdu and Persian poet, Mirza Asadullah Baig Khan (Mirza Ghalib, 1797-1869), lived his final, most creatively fruitful years; housing Ghalib Ki Haveli, a conserved 19th-century brick-and-mortar residence converted by the Delhi Government into a literary museum displaying Ghalib's handwritten couplets, vintage hookahs, life-size bust, and personal letters.

name: Bhuli Bhatiyari Ka Mahal Central Ridge
description: Hidden deep inside the dense, rocky forest of the Central Delhi Ridge near Jhandewalan and Southern Ridge Reserve Forest, constructed in the 14th century by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq, Bhuli Bhatiyari Ka Mahal was originally a fortified royal hunting lodge ('shikargah') and retreat, featuring an imposing double-entry stone gateway, thick rubble stone battlements, an inner courtyard, and a water reservoir bund, surrounded by centuries of local ghost legends and folklore.

name: Central Baptist Church Chandni Chowk (1814)
description: Standing on Chandni Chowk just opposite Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib, established in 1814 by the Baptist Missionary Society of London, Central Baptist Church is celebrated as the oldest surviving Christian church in northern India, built in an elegant European neoclassical style featuring a grand portico supported by eight heavy circular columns, deep verandas, a pitched roof, and memorial stone plaques documenting 19th-century missionary and Indian Christian history through the 1857 uprising.

name: Chandni Chowk
description: Designed in 1650 by Princess Jahanara Begum, one of India's oldest and busiest bazaars stretching from the Red Fort to Fatehpuri Mosque, newly revitalized with red sandstone pedestrian plazas.

name: Dariba Kalan, Kinari Bazaar & Paranthe Wali Gali
description: Branching southward from the central artery of Chandni Chowk, this interconnected network of historic 17th-century pedestrian alleys forms the cultural soul of Shahjahanabad: Dariba Kalan ('Street of Incomparable Pearl') has traded in pure silver jewelry, antique coins, and traditional attar perfumes since 1650; Kinari Bazaar is India's premier wedding embellishment alley overflowing with zari borders, gold lace, and turbans; and Gali Paranthe Wali is the world-famous culinary lane celebrated since the 1870s for deep-fried stuffed flatbreads.

name: Diwan-i-Am (Hall of Public Audience) Red Fort
description: Situated within the central inner courtyard of the UNESCO World Heritage Red Fort, constructed in 1648 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, Diwan-i-Am is an imposing red sandstone hall fronted by 27 open multi-cusped arched bays supported by triple columns, featuring the Emperor's elevated white marble throne canopy ('Jharokha-i-Khas') backed by exquisite Florentine pietra dura marble relief panels depicting birds, flowers, and Orpheus playing the lute.

name: Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience) Red Fort
description: Situated on the eastern riverfront terrace of the Red Fort, constructed in 1648 from pure Makrana white marble, Diwan-i-Khas was the inner sanctum of Mughal state diplomacy, adorned with gold-leaf ceiling carvings, semi-precious stone floral inlays, and the immortal Persian couplet by Amir Khusrau inscribed in gold: 'Gar firdaus bar roo-e zameen ast, hameen ast-o hameen ast-o hameen ast' (If there is a paradise on earth, it is this, it is this, it is this), where the gem-studded Peacock Throne once stood before being plundered by Nadir Shah in 1739.

name: Fatehpuri Masjid & Historic Spice Courtyard
description: Marking the western visual terminus of Chandni Chowk directly opposite the Red Fort across a 1.5-km axis, constructed in 1650 CE by Fatehpuri Begum (one of Emperor Shah Jahan's royal wives), Fatehpuri Masjid is an imposing red sandstone congregational mosque built on an elevated plinth, featuring a single fluted central dome, soaring minarets, seven arched prayer bays, and an expansive courtyard with a central ablution pool where spice traders and pilgrims find quiet respite from the bustling markets of Khari Baoli.

name: Firoz Shah Kotla Citadel & Ashokan Pillar of Topra
description: Occupying a dramatic historical site along Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg near ITO, constructed in 1354 CE by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq as the fortified citadel of Firozabad (the fifth historic city of Delhi), this sprawling stone fortress features the world-renowned 3rd-century BCE polished sandstone Ashokan Pillar of Topra (transported 180 km from Haryana in 1356 aboard a 42-wheel cart pulled by 8,400 men and re-erected atop a three-tiered stepped pyramid), subterranean chambers, and lush green lawns.

name: Gauri Shankar Mandir Chandni Chowk
description: Situated near the Red Fort intersection along the main thoroughfare of Chandni Chowk, Gauri Shankar Mandir is an 800-year-old historic Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, founded according to temple tradition by a wounded Maratha soldier named Appa Gangadhar who vowed to build a temple if he survived battle, featuring a revered 800-year-old natural brown lingam encased in silver phallus sheets, an ornate silver canopy, and golden temple spires.

name: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib Chandni Chowk
description: Standing majestically in central Chandni Chowk, constructed in 1783 by Sardar Baghel Singh to commemorate the supreme martyrdom of the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur (who was beheaded here on 11 November 1675 by order of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb for defending the religious freedom of Kashmiri Pandits), Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib is one of the holiest Sikh gurdwaras in India, featuring a gleaming golden dome, an ornate white marble sanctum, the preserved trunk of the banyan tree beneath which the Guru was martyred, and a 24-hour community kitchen (Guru ka Langar).

name: Hayat Bakhsh Bagh & Sawan-Bhadon Pavilions Red Fort
description: Occupying the northeastern quarter of the Red Fort, Hayat Bakhsh Bagh ('Life-Bestowing Garden') is a formal Mughal Charbagh laid out by Shah Jahan in 1648, centered around a large water reservoir featuring the red sandstone Zafar Mahal (built in 1842 by the last Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar II), flanked at either end by the elegant white marble pavilions of Sawan and Bhadon, named after the monsoon months and designed with niches for flickering candles behind cascading water sheets.

name: Historic Gates of Shahjahanabad (Kashmere, Ajmeri, Delhi & Turkman)
description: Dating from 1638-1648 CE when Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan built the monumental 6-kilometer stone wall enclosing his capital Shahjahanabad, these surviving historic stone city gates include Kashmere Gate (with dual arched portals famously blown open by British sappers on 14 September 1857), Ajmeri Gate (oriented southwest toward Ajmer with heavy wooden leaves), Delhi Gate (flanked by stone elephants and heavy bastions), and Turkman Gate (named after the 13th-century Sufi saint Hazrat Shah Turkman Bayabani).

name: Jama Masjid Delhi
description: Commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1656, an immense red sandstone and white marble mosque with a vast courtyard accommodating 25,000 worshippers, flanked by two 40-meter minarets.

name: Jami Masjid of Firozabad & Circular Baoli
description: Situated within the northern sector of Firoz Shah Kotla, the monumental Jami Masjid was commenced in 1354 CE on a high vaulted plinth overlooking the Yamuna, so magnificent that the Turco-Mongol conqueror Timur prayed here in 1398 and was inspired to take Delhi stone-masons back to Samarkand to build the Bibi-Khanym Mosque; directly adjacent lies Delhi's only surviving circular stepwell (Circular Baoli), an engineering marvel featuring subterranean chambers and concentric stepped terraces surrounding a central deep well shaft.

name: Jhandewalan Mandir (Maa Aadi Shakti Shrine)
description: Situated on Desh Bandhu Gupta Road near Karol Bagh in central Delhi, Jhandewalan Mandir is one of Delhi's most celebrated historic temples dedicated to Maa Aadi Shakti, named after the ceremonial prayer flags ('jhandas') hoisted here in the 18th century by the devout merchant Badri Bhagat after he excavated the ancient subterranean idol of the Goddess from a secluded cave on the ridge, featuring multi-tiered marble prayer halls, an underground sanctum cave ('Gufa'), and radiant golden deity embellishments.

name: Khari Baoli (Asia's Largest Wholesale Spice Market)
description: Sprawling adjacent to Fatehpuri Masjid along Khari Baoli road in Old Delhi, operating continuously since the 17th century when it was established during Shah Jahan's reign, Khari Baoli is universally celebrated as Asia's largest wholesale spice market, an overwhelming sensory wonderland packed with hundreds of historic trading shops and multi-storey haveli warehouses ('Gadodia Market') stacked to the ceilings with towering burlap sacks of pungent dried red chilies, turmeric, saffron, cardamom, cloves, and exotic herbs.

name: Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) Red Fort
description: Tucked discreetly inside the Red Fort royal enclosure adjacent to the Hammam, constructed between 1659 and 1660 by Emperor Aurangzeb as his private place of personal prayer, Moti Masjid ('Pearl Mosque') is a jewel of late Mughal architecture, enclosed within high red sandstone walls and crafted entirely of polished white and grey-veined Makrana marble, featuring three bulbous onion domes, miniature chattris, curved Bengali-style eaves, and an elevated marble courtyard.

name: National Children's Museum & National Bal Bhavan
description: Sprawling across 12 lush acres on Kotla Road near ITO, founded in 1956 at the personal initiative of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, the National Bal Bhavan and National Children's Museum is India's premier creative institution for children, featuring a working mini diesel toy train circling the campus, an interactive science park, a traffic training park, an aviary, and museum galleries displaying international children's art, traditional Indian toys, musical instruments, and cultural puppets.

name: National Gandhi Museum & Library Raj Ghat
description: Situated directly opposite the Raj Ghat memorial park along Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, established in 1961, the National Gandhi Museum is India's principal memorial institution dedicated to the life, thought, and martyrdom of Mahatma Gandhi, preserving an incomparable collection of over 75,000 books, original handwritten letters, spinning wheels (charkhas), his pocket watch, walking stick, spectacles, and the blood-stained dhoti and shawl he wore on the day of his assassination on 30 January 1948, alongside rare audio recordings of his speeches.

name: National Science Centre Delhi
description: Inaugurated in 1992 near Gate No. 1 of Pragati Maidan, one of the largest interactive science museums in Asia, featuring eight floors of hands-on interactive galleries, a 3D theater, dinosaur gallery, and the iconic rolling Energy Ball demonstration.

name: National Zoological Park Delhi
description: Established in 1959 beside Purana Qila, housing over 1,300 animals across 127 species in natural moated island enclosures, renowned for successful royal Bengal white tiger and Sangai deer breeding programs.

name: Naubat Khana & Chatta Chowk Covered Bazaar Red Fort
description: Entered immediately past the monumental Lahori Gate of the Red Fort, Chatta Chowk (or Meena Bazaar) is a 17th-century two-storey covered arcaded brick bazaar inspired by the silk markets of Isfahan where imperial merchants once sold brocades, silks, and jewels to court ladies, leading directly to the Naubat Khana ('Drum House' or Hathiapol), an ornate red sandstone gatehouse where royal musicians played kettle drums five times daily and nobles dismounted from their elephants before entering the emperor's presence.

name: Purana Qila (Old Fort)
description: Built on the ancient mound of Mahabharata's Indraprastha, reconstructed by Sher Shah Suri and Humayun in the 16th century, featuring massive stone ramparts, Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque, and Sher Mandal observatory.

name: Raj Ghat (Mahatma Gandhi Memorial)
description: A black marble platform surrounded by landscaped lawns and an eternal flame on the banks of the Yamuna River, marking the sacred spot where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated on January 31, 1948.

name: Rang Mahal & Mumtaz Mahal Red Fort
description: Occupying the riverfront residential axis of the Red Fort, Rang Mahal ('Palace of Colors') was the royal imperial seraglio for the emperor's consorts, renowned for its gilded ceiling, mirrored glass walls, and a central white marble fountain basin carved in the form of an open lotus fed by the cooling waters of the Nahr-i-Bihisht (Stream of Paradise), while the adjacent Mumtaz Mahal today houses the Red Fort Archaeological Museum showcasing Mughal-era arms, textiles, and celadon pottery.

name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
description: Built in 1648 by Shah Jahan as the palace fort of Shahjahanabad, an UNESCO World Heritage citadel of red sandstone with monumental ramparts, Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, and the Lahore Gate where the Prime Minister addresses the nation on Independence Day.

name: Salimgarh Fort
description: Built in 1546 by Salim Shah Suri on an island in the Yamuna River, later linked to the Red Fort by a bridge, used as a prison where Aurangzeb imprisoned his sister Roshanara and the British held Indian National Army (INA) officers.

name: Shankar's International Dolls Museum ITO
description: Situated in the Children's Book Trust building on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg near ITO, established in 1965 by the pioneering political cartoonist K. Shankar Pillai, Shankar's International Dolls Museum is one of the world's most comprehensive collections of international costume dolls, displaying over 7,000 authentic handcrafted dolls from more than 85 nations across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas, alongside regional Indian traditional bridal, classical dance, and tribal costume dolls.

name: Shri Digambar Jain Lal Mandir & Birds Charitable Hospital
description: Standing directly opposite the Red Fort at the eastern terminus of Chandni Chowk, founded in 1656 during the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan by an imperial army officer, Shri Digambar Jain Lal Mandir is the oldest and best-known Jain temple in Delhi, constructed of luminous red sandstone, dedicated to the 23rd Tirthankara Lord Parshvanatha, celebrated across the world for housing the unique Birds Charitable Hospital in its rear courtyard, which treats and rehabilitates over 15,000 injured wild and domestic birds annually completely free of cost.

name: Town Hall of Old Delhi & Victoria Square
description: Occupying a prominent garden square along the northern side of Chandni Chowk, completed in 1866 as the Lawrence Institute and subsequently serving as the municipal headquarters of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) for over a century, Town Hall is an imposing Victorian yellow-brick and sandstone landmark featuring arched colonnades, Corinthian pediments, and a central square where a colossal bronze statue of Queen Victoria once stood (later replaced by the statue of Arya Samaj leader Swami Shraddhanand).

name: EOD Adventure Park Sanjay Lake (Zip-Line & Boating)
description: Situated along the scenic waterfront of Sanjay Lake in Mayur Vihar Phase II in East Delhi, operated in partnership with the DDA, EOD ('Every Other Day') Adventure Park is Delhi's premier multi-activity outdoor adventure destination, featuring Delhi's longest over-water zip-line, tree-top obstacle rope courses, professional archery ranges, bowling alleys, paintball arenas, body zorb balls, pedal boating on the lake, and dedicated kids' adventure zones.

name: Sanjay Lake & Boating Park Mayur Vihar
description: Stretching across 17 hectares (42 acres) within a 69-hectare landscaped park in Mayur Vihar Phase II in East Delhi, developed in the 1970s by the DDA, Sanjay Lake is a vast artificial freshwater lake fed by rainwater runoff, featuring pedal and row boating facilities, shaded walking and fitness promenades, a dedicated children's play area, and serving as a seasonal resting haven for indigenous waterbirds such as cormorants, common teals, and spot-billed ducks.

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple Delhi
description: Inaugurated in 2005, a colossal 100-acre temple complex built from carved pink Rajasthani sandstone and Italian Carrara marble without using steel, featuring 234 carved pillars, 9 domes, and 20,000 carved sculptures.

name: Agrasen ki Baoli
description: A 60-meter long and 15-meter wide ancient stepwell on Hailey Road believed to be originally built by legendary King Agrasen and rebuilt in the 14th century, featuring 108 stone steps descending through arched niches.

name: Amrit Udyan (Mughal Gardens Pavilion)
description: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens combining Mughal charbagh canal architecture with English country cottage flowerbeds, featuring 159 varieties of roses, circular butterfly gardens, and cascading fountains inside Rashtrapati Bhavan.

name: Bara Gumbad & Mohammad Shah Tomb
description: The monumental 1444 tomb of Sayyid ruler Muhammad Shah and the colossal Bara Gumbad (Big Dome) gateway constructed in 1494 with an attached three-domed mosque adorned with exquisite Arabic stucco calligraphy.

name: Birla Mandir (Laxminarayan Temple Mandir Marg)
description: Situated on Mandir Marg west of Connaught Place, constructed between 1933 and 1939 by industrialist Baldeo Das Birla and his sons, Laxminarayan Temple (popularly known as Birla Mandir) was the first large-scale Hindu temple erected in modern Delhi, inaugurated in 1939 by Mahatma Gandhi on the strict condition that it must remain open to people of all castes, creeds, and faiths without discrimination, featuring red sandstone and marble Nagara shikhara spires soaring 49 meters, exquisite frescoes, and landscaped gardens with waterfalls.

name: Buddha Jayanti Park Southern Ridge
description: Sprawling across 81 rolling acres of the forested Southern Ridge on Vandemataram Marg, laid out in 1956 to celebrate the 2,500th anniversary of Gautama Buddha's Mahaparinirvana, this beautifully landscaped park features rolling grassy hillocks, babbling artificial streams, rocky outcrops, an island pavilion dedicated by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1993 enshrining a gilded Buddha statue, and a sacred Bodhi tree sapling planted by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1964, brought as a cutting from Sri Lanka's historic Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi.

name: Cathedral Church of the Redemption
description: Designed by Henry Medd and opened in 1931 near Rashtrapati Bhavan, an elegant colonial church featuring massive red sandstone arches, high domes, and historic pipe organs.

name: Connaught Place (Rajiv Chowk)
description: Constructed between 1929 and 1933, a grand Georgian-style circular market with three rings (Inner, Middle, Outer) lined with monumental white colonnades, flagship global brands, underground Palika Bazaar, and historic cafes.

name: Delhi Golf Club (Historic 18-Hole Course with Lodi Tombs)
description: Sprawling across 220 historic acres on Dr. Zakir Hussain Marg near Delhi Zoo and Lodhi Gardens, established in the 1930s and designed as an international 18-hole championship course, the Delhi Golf Club is globally unique: its rolling green fairways are studded with over 30 ancient, protected 15th-century Lodi and Mughal tombs, arched gateways, and pavilions (including the Tomb of Sayed Abid and Lal Bangla), while the surrounding mature forest shelters over 300 species of resident and migratory birds.

name: Delhi Metro Museum Patel Chowk
description: Located inside the concourse of Patel Chowk Metro Station on the Yellow Line, inaugurated in December 2008 by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), this is South Asia's first transit museum housed inside a working underground metro station, showcasing the engineering triumphs, tunnel-boring technology, soil management feats, historical development, and operational milestones of the world's most advanced urban mass transit system.

name: Gandhi Smriti Museum (Birla House)
description: The historic mansion where Mahatma Gandhi spent the final 144 days of his life and where he was assassinated on January 30, 1948, now housing the Eternal Gandhi multimedia exhibition and preserved bedroom.

name: Gurudwara Rakab Ganj Sahib (Guru Tegh Bahadur Cremation Site)
description: Standing on Pandit Pant Marg directly opposite the Parliament House complex, constructed in 1783 by Sikh military leader Sardar Baghel Singh, Gurudwara Rakab Ganj Sahib marks the deeply sacred historical site where the headless mortal remains of the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, were cremated under cover of darkness on 11 November 1675 by his devout disciple Lakhi Shah Vanjara, who burned down his own house to cremate the Guru's body without arousing the suspicion of Mughal guards, featuring an exquisite white Makrana marble palace surrounded by formal lawns.

name: Gurudwara Sri Bangla Sahib
description: Associated with the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan Ji, who stayed here in 1664 healing cholera victims, featuring a gleaming golden dome, a sacred curative water pool (sarovar), and a mega-langar kitchen.

name: India Gate & National War Memorial
description: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens in 1931, an iconic 42-meter triumphal arch commemorating 84,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army, adjacent to the concentric underground circles of the National War Memorial.

name: Indira Gandhi Memorial Museum
description: The former official bungalow residence of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, preserved as a public memorial museum showcasing her living rooms, study, personal library, and the glass pathway marking her final walk in 1984.

name: Jantar Mantar Delhi
description: Constructed in 1724 by Maharaja Jai Singh II of Jaipur, an open-air astronomical observatory consisting of 13 colossal architectural astronomy instruments designed to compile astronomical tables and predict eclipses.

name: Lodhi Garden
description: A historic 90-acre park protecting grand 15th-century stone monuments of the Sayyid and Lodi dynasties (Bara Gumbad, Shisha Gumbad, Sikandar Lodi Tomb) set amidst manicured lawns, botanical trees, and rose gardens.

name: Mahipalpur Hunting Lodge of Firoz Shah Tughlaq
description: Standing on a high natural rocky ridge in Mahipalpur village near Delhi International Airport, constructed around 1370 CE by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq, this imposing rubble stone hunting palace (Mahal) features an arched three-bay hall, vaulted corner pavilions, stone bastions, and a massive earthen-and-stone bund (embankment dam) that historically trapped rain runoff from the Aravalli hills to form a seasonal lake attracting waterfowl and wild game for royal hunting expeditions.

name: Malcha Mahal (Sultanate Hunting Lodge) Central Ridge
description: Concealed deep in the wilderness of the Southern Ridge near the Earth Station on Malcha Marg, constructed around 1325 CE by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Malcha Mahal (historically known as Wilayat Mahal) is a secluded rubble stone hunting palace built atop a rocky volcanic outcrop, featuring three arched bays, a massive stone terrace, and vaulted halls, famously shrouded in modern tragedy as the reclusive sanctuary where the eccentric self-proclaimed royal family of Oudh (Begum Wilayat Mahal and Prince Ali Raza) lived in total isolation for decades.

name: National Crafts Museum & Hastkala Academy Pragati Maidan
description: Situated near Purana Qila on Bhairon Marg, established in 1956 and designed by legendary architect Charles Correa, the National Crafts Museum & Hastkala Academy is one of India's largest and most vibrant ethnographic cultural centers, housing over 35,000 rare traditional tribal and folk artifacts, textiles, terracotta sculptures, wooden temple chariots, and brass metalwork, featuring a charming Village Complex with authentic mud-and-thatch rural dwellings from different Indian states where master craftspeople demonstrate traditional weaving, pottery, and metal casting live.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA Jaipur House)
description: Situated at the India Gate hexagon, housed in the opulent 1936 butterfly-shaped neoclassical palace of the Maharaja of Jaipur ('Jaipur House'), the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) is India's premier institution for modern and contemporary visual art, preserving an extraordinary collection of over 17,000 artworks spanning from the mid-19th century to the present, including iconic masterpieces by Raja Ravi Varma, Amrita Sher-Gil, Rabindranath Tagore, Nandalal Bose, Jamini Roy, and M.F. Husain.

name: National Museum New Delhi
description: Established in 1949, India's premier museum holding over 200,000 works of art spanning five millennia, including the famous Harappan Dancing Girl, Buddhist sacred relics, miniature paintings, and Tanjore art.

name: National Museum of Natural History (FICCI / MoEFCC)
description: Operating under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), this premier educational institution is devoted to environmental education and biodiversity awareness, presenting temporary and traveling exhibitions, hands-on discovery rooms, interactive wildlife dioramas, botanical fossil casts, and ecological models highlighting the fragile marine and terrestrial ecosystems of the Indian subcontinent.

name: National Philatelic Museum Dak Bhawan
description: Situated on the ground floor of Dak Bhawan on Sansad Marg (Parliament Street) near Patel Chowk, operated by the Department of Posts, the National Philatelic Museum is India's flagship postal museum, housing an extraordinary chronological collection of thousands of rare postage stamps, including the historic Scinde Dawk (Asia's first adhesive stamp issued in 1852), the 1854 Four Annas two-colored lithograph, pre-independence Princely State postal issues, Mahatma Gandhi 1948 memorial stamps, and vintage post-boxes.

name: National Rail Museum New Delhi
description: Spread over 11 acres in Chanakyapuri, India's premier rail museum showcasing the 1855 Fairy Queen (world's oldest working steam locomotive), royal salon cars of the Maharajas, and an operating outdoor 1:8 scale heritage joy train.

name: Nehru Park Chanakyapuri
description: An 80-acre undulating landscaped park in the diplomatic heart of Chanakyapuri, featuring sprawling lawns, blooming seasonal flowers, and a natural amphitheater hosting prestigious morning classical music concerts.

name: Pracheen Hanuman Mandir Connaught Place (Pandava Era)
description: Situated on Baba Kharak Singh Marg near Connaught Place, Pracheen Hanuman Mandir is revered as one of the five original temples of Delhi founded by the Pandavas after the Kurukshetra war in the Mahabharata, extensively renovated in 1724 by Maharaja Jai Singh II of Jaipur, famous for its south-facing idol of Lord Hanuman, its silver-embossed ceilings, its Guinness World Record 24-hour continuous chanting of the 'Sri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram' mantra unbroken since 1 August 1964, and the vibrant henna (mehndi) artists lining its outer veranda.

name: Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya & Nehru Planetarium (Teen Murti)
description: Sprawling across the historic 25-acre Teen Murti Estate (the former residence of Commander-in-Chief of the British Indian Army and later of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru), inaugurated in April 2022, Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya is a cutting-edge technological and biographical museum honoring the contributions of every Prime Minister of India since 1947, featuring interactive holographic displays, virtual reality time-travel rides, kinetic art installations, and the historic Nehru Memorial Museum, alongside the Nehru Planetarium presenting sky theatre astronomical shows.

name: Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque Purana Qila
description: Standing majestically within the inner lawns of Purana Qila, constructed in 1541 CE by Afghan Emperor Sher Shah Suri, Qila-i-Kuhna ('Mosque of the Old Fort') is universally recognized by architectural historians as the glorious pinnacle of the pre-Mughal Sultanate style, featuring a five-bay facade adorned with sharply delineated horseshoe arches, multi-colored marble and red sandstone inlays, calligraphic bands, jharokha balconies, and an interior central dome of breathtaking proportions.

name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
description: Completed in 1929, the monumental 340-room neoclassical mansion designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens on Raisina Hill, one of the largest presidential residences in the world, featuring the copper-domed Durbar Hall.

name: Safdarjung Tomb
description: Built in 1754 for Nawab Safdarjung, Prime Minister of the Mughal Empire, the last monumental charbagh garden tomb of the Mughal style, featuring red and brownish-yellow sandstone and nine-fold floor plans.

name: Samvidhan Sadan (Old Parliament House)
description: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and Sir Herbert Baker and opened in 1927, the iconic circular colonnaded building with 144 granite pillars where the Constitution of India was drafted and adopted.

name: Sher Mandal (Humayun's Astronomical Library Observatory)
description: Standing on the highest elevation within Purana Qila, originally commenced by Sher Shah Suri and completed around 1555 by Mughal Emperor Humayun as his personal astronomical observatory and royal library, Sher Mandal is an elegant two-storey octagonal red sandstone and white marble tower crowned by a domed chhatri, renowned in Indian history as the fateful site where on 24 January 1556 Humayun, rushing down the steep stone stairs upon hearing the evening call to prayer (Azan), slipped on his robe and died from his injuries.

name: Sher Shah Suri Gate (Lal Darwaza) & Khair-ul-Manazil
description: Standing on Mathura Road directly opposite the entrance to Purana Qila, Lal Darwaza (Sher Shah Suri Gate) is a monumental red sandstone and local quartzite gateway built around 1540 as the northern ceremonial portal to Sher Shah's fortified city of Shergarh; directly adjacent stands Khair-ul-Manazil ('Auspicious of Houses'), a magnificent two-storey madrasa and mosque complex built in 1561 by Maham Anga (Akbar's influential wet-nurse and foster mother), famous historically as the site where an assassin shot an arrow at Emperor Akbar in 1564.

name: Sikandar Lodi Tomb
description: Built in 1517 by his son Ibrahim Lodi, the fortified tomb of Sultan Sikandar Lodi, notable in Indian architectural history as the earliest surviving monument featuring a double dome within an enclosed garden.

name: Supreme Court Museum of India
description: Situated within the majestic Supreme Court complex on Tilak Marg, inaugurated in 2004, the Supreme Court Museum of India documents the profound evolutionary history of the Indian justice system from ancient Ashokan and Dharmashastra jurisprudence to Mughal royal decrees (firmans), British colonial High Courts, and the modern constitutional court, displaying rare original legal manuscripts, authentic seals of Mughal qazis, courtroom wigs, and original copies of landmark historic verdicts.

name: Coronation Memorial Delhi
description: The historic ceremonial amphitheater where King George V and Queen Mary were proclaimed Emperor and Empress of India in the 1911 Delhi Durbar, and where the shift of India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi was announced.

name: Dara Shikoh Library Building Kashmere Gate
description: Situated within the Kashmere Gate campus of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University, originally built in 1637 CE as the private riverside palace library of Prince Dara Shikoh (the erudite eldest son of Shah Jahan who translated the Upanishads into Persian as 'Sirr-i-Akbar'), this layered historic monument was later transformed in 1803 into the British Residency of Sir David Ochterlony with classical Corinthian colonnades, subsequently housing Delhi College, and today meticulously conserved by the Delhi Archaeology Department as the Museum of Delhi's City History.

name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Memorial 26 Alipur Road
description: Standing on 26 Alipur Road in Civil Lines, constructed on the sacred site where the Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution, Bharat Ratna Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, lived his final years and attained Mahaparinirvana on 6 December 1956, dedicated to the nation in April 2018, this monumental memorial is engineered in the symbolic architectural form of an open book representing the Constitution of India, featuring interactive digital galleries, life-size animatronics, personal belongings, and a tranquil meditation hall.

name: Flagstaff Tower Northern Ridge
description: Standing on the highest natural elevation of the Northern Ridge within the Kamla Nehru Ridge Forest, built around 1828 by the British Indian military as a signal tower and cantonment lookout, Flagstaff Tower is a circular, castellated one-storey brick and plaster bastion that played a dramatic role on 11 May 1857, when surviving British officers, women, and children fled here under siege from the mutinous Sepoy troops in Old Delhi, holding out desperately until dusk before fleeing on horse-carts toward Karnal and Ambala.

name: Gurudwara Majnu Ka Tilla (Yamuna Riverbank Shrine)
description: Perched on an elevated natural mound overlooking the Yamuna River along the Ring Road in North Delhi, founded in the late 15th century during the reign of Sultan Sikandar Lodi, Gurudwara Majnu Ka Tilla commemorates the sacred site where the first Sikh Guru, Guru Nanak Dev Ji, met and spiritually enlightened the Iranian Muslim hermit Abdullah (nicknamed 'Majnu' for his ecstatic devotion), and where the sixth Sikh Guru, Guru Hargobind Ji, camped during his stay in Delhi in the 17th century at the invitation of Emperor Jahangir.

name: Kamla Nehru Ridge Forest & Biodiversity Trails
description: Encompassing 87 hectares of historic protected forest on the Northern Ridge bordering Delhi University North Campus, Kamla Nehru Ridge is an oasis of dense urban woodland preserving centuries-old dhau, neem, and keekar canopies, interconnected walking and jogging trails, vibrant bird populations (including flycatchers, parakeets, and owls), and historic colonial landmarks including Khooni Khan Lake, the British Flagstaff Tower, and Chauburji Mosque.

name: Mutiny Memorial (Ajitgarh) Northern Ridge
description: Rising 33 meters (108 feet) above the forested crest of the Northern Ridge on Rani Jhansi Road near Hindu Rao Hospital, erected in 1863 by the British Public Works Department in the Victorian Gothic style, this octagonal red sandstone spire resembles a medieval cathedral bell-tower, adorned with marble inscription plaques recording the military casualties of the 1857 Siege of Delhi, rededicated in 1972 on the 25th anniversary of Indian Independence as 'Ajitgarh' with an inscription honoring Indian freedom fighters who fell resisting colonial rule.

name: Qudsia Bagh & 18th-Century Baradari
description: Situated on Shamnath Marg near Kashmere Gate, laid out in 1748 CE by Qudsia Begum (the consort of Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela' and mother of Emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur), Qudsia Bagh was a lavish 50-acre Persian-style riverfront pleasure garden, preserving its monumental double-storey red sandstone entrance gateway, an intact 18th-century stone baradari (pleasure pavilion with 12 arched openings), an ornate three-domed royal mosque, and expansive green lawns that played a pivotal strategic role as a British artillery battery position during the 1857 Siege of Delhi.

name: Roshanara Garden & Tomb of Roshanara Begum
description: Sprawling across a vast leafy expanse in north Delhi near Subzi Mandi, laid out in 1650 CE by Princess Roshanara Begum (the brilliant, politically influential second daughter of Emperor Shah Jahan and fierce supporter of Aurangzeb during the Mughal war of succession), this historic Mughal charbagh garden surrounds her open-air white marble tomb pavilion, featuring an ornate central baradari with fluted arches, carved stone jali screens, tranquil water channels, ancient trees, and the historic Roshanara Cricket Club (where the BCCI was founded in 1928).

name: St. James' Church (Skinner's Church)
description: Consecrated in 1836 by Colonel James Skinner in gratitude for surviving the battle of Uniara, an elegant neoclassical cruciform church with an octagonal dome, copper cross, and historic European graves.

name: Wazirabad Mosque, Tomb & Firoz Shah's Bridge
description: Situated on the banks of the Yamuna River in North Delhi near the Wazirabad Barrage, this remarkable medieval complex was founded in the late 14th century by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq, comprising a multi-arched stone bridge-cum-weir spanning a former Yamuna tributary, an ornate three-domed mosque with projecting jharokha balconies, and the serene open-air white-domed tomb of the revered 14th-century Sufi saint Shah Alam (known affectionately as 'Chhote Shah Alam').

name: Yamuna Biodiversity Park Wazirabad
description: Situated on the active floodplain of the Yamuna River near Wazirabad in North Delhi, spanning 457 acres of restored wetlands, grasslands, and riverine riparian forests, Yamuna Biodiversity Park is an internationally acclaimed ecological conservation triumph developed by DDA and Delhi University scientists, featuring two large engineered shallow wetlands that host up to 5,000 migratory waterfowl annually (including northern pintails, ferruginous poachers, and bar-headed geese), a herbal garden, and a fruit conservatory.

name: Adventure Island & Metro Walk Rohini
description: Sprawling across 62 acres adjacent to Rithala Metro Station in Rohini Sector 10, Adventure Island is a premier world-class amusement theme park and open-air retail promenade ('Metro Walk'), featuring 25 thrilling international-standard rides (including the Z-Force drop tower, Twister roller coaster, Lightning Bug, and Sky Riders), a large man-made water lagoon, splash pools, water coasters, and an entertainment boardwalk lined with waterfront restaurants.

name: Bawana Zail Historic Fortress Delhi
description: Standing prominently in the historic village center of Bawana in northwest Delhi, constructed around the 1860s during the British colonial era by the local revenue heads ('Zaildars'), Bawana Zail (or Bawana Jail) is a unique fortified brick compound featuring towering corner bastions, rifle loopholes, heavy iron-plated wooden gates, and arched prison lock-ups, which later served as a secret base for Indian freedom fighters during the 1942 Quit India Movement.

name: Dilli Haat Pitampura & Janakpuri Cultural Bazaars
description: Comprising Delhi Tourism's two sister cultural haat complexes in North and West Delhi—Dilli Haat Pitampura (adjoining TV Tower on 7.2 acres with an amphitheatre, spice court, and art gallery) and Dilli Haat Janakpuri (spanning 8 acres designed with modern bamboo pavilions, a 800-seat outdoor amphitheatre, and 100 craft stalls)—these expansive centers provide vibrant regional venues for live folk music festivals, handicraft exhibitions, and pan-Indian culinary events.

name: Guru Tegh Bahadur Memorial Singhu Border GT Karnal Road
description: Occupying an expansive 20-acre landscaped complex along National Highway 44 (GT Karnal Road) near the Singhu border in North West Delhi, constructed in 2011 by the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC), this monumental national memorial honors Guru Tegh Bahadur, featuring a central red sandstone pylon soaring 24 meters into the sky representing the Guru, surrounded by ten radiating petal-shaped brick and stone monoliths symbolizing the ten Sikh Gurus and their eternal teachings.

name: Shalimar Garden & Sheesh Mahal (Aurangzeb's Coronation Site)
description: Situated in Shalimar Bagh in northwest Delhi, laid out in 1653 CE by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Izz-un-Nisa Begum (Akbarabadi Mahal) as an imperial staging camp on the Grand Trunk Road to Lahore and Kashmir, this lavish Mughal garden is renowned in world history as the exact site where Emperor Aurangzeb had his royal coronation ceremony on 31 July 1658 following the defeat of his brother Dara Shikoh, preserving the elegant Sheesh Mahal pavilion adorned with painted floral ceilings, arched verandas, and cascading water terraces.

name: Adham Khan's Tomb (Bhool Bhulaiya Mehrauli)
description: Perched on the ancient ramparts of Lal Kot just north of Mehrauli bus terminal, commissioned in 1562 CE by Mughal Emperor Akbar for his foster-brother and general Adham Khan (whom Akbar had thrown twice from the Agra Fort terrace for assassinating Prime Minister Atgah Khan), this imposing gray stone and red sandstone octagonal tomb is built in the Sur/Lodi style rather than contemporary Mughal style (a deliberate architectural slight by Akbar), locally called 'Bhool Bhulaiya' ('The Labyrinth') due to a maze of narrow vaulted passageways concealed within the thickness of its upper dome walls.

name: Alai Darwaza & Alai Minar Qutub Complex
description: Situated within the southern and northern sectors of the Qutub Complex, built in 1311 CE by Sultan Alauddin Khalji, Alai Darwaza is the celebrated southern ceremonial gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, hailed by art historians as the first monument in India built with true arches, true domes, and Islamic horseshoe arched screens carved in red sandstone and white marble; while to the north stands the massive rubble core of the Alai Minar, conceived by Khalji to stand twice as tall as the Qutub Minar (at 145 meters) before his death in 1316 halted construction at 24.5 meters.

name: Anangtal Baoli & Ancient Tomar Reservoir
description: Tucked in the dense forest grove behind the Qutub Complex within Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Anangtal is an ancient 11th-century stone step-reservoir engineered by the Rajput King Anangpal II Tomar around 1060 CE (the monarch who founded Lal Kot, Delhi's first historic fortified city), featuring ancient dressed quartzite block masonry, terraced steps descending to a natural catchment basin, and recently declared a Monument of National Importance by the Government of India in 2022.

name: Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary & Surajkund Slopes
description: Sprawling across 6,874 acres (27.8 sq km) of the rugged southern Aravalli ridge on the Delhi-Haryana border near Tughlaqabad, the Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary is Delhi's largest and wildest protected wilderness, supporting dry deciduous scrub forests, deep quartzite ravines, and spectacular sapphire-blue flooded quarry lakes (including Neelkanth Lake and Bhardwaj Lake), serving as a thriving habitat for confirmed breeding populations of wild leopards, striped hyenas, golden jackals, blackbucks, and the Conservation Education Centre (CEC).

name: Bade Khan & Chhote Khan Tombs Kotla Mubarakpur
description: Rising majestically from a manicured garden park in South Extension adjacent to Kotla Mubarakpur, constructed during the Lodi period in the late 15th century, Bade Khan and Chhote Khan ('Big Lord and Small Lord') are twin monumental stone mausoleums celebrated by architectural historians for their sophisticated transitional design between Lodi and Mughal styles, featuring soaring central domes, decorative three-tiered facade arches giving the illusion of multi-storeys, and ornate octagonal corner turrets.

name: Balban's Tomb & Dar-ul-Aman Ruins Mehrauli
description: Standing amid ancient keekar trees in Mehrauli Archaeological Park, constructed in 1287 CE, this ruined rubble masonry tomb of Sultan Ghiyas-ud-din Balban (the fierce Mamluk ruler who consolidated the Delhi Sultanate) marks a monumental milestone in the history of Indian architecture: its four entranceways contain the earliest extant 'true arches' (arches with radiating voussoirs and keystones) ever constructed in the Indian subcontinent, set within the ruins of the medieval sanctuary known as 'Dar-ul-Aman' (Haven of Safety).

name: Begumpur Mosque
description: Built around 1351 by Khan-i-Jahan Junan Shah, prime minister of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, a colossal stone mosque in the medieval city of Jahanpanah featuring 64 domed bays and a monumental pishtaq arch.

name: Bijay Mandal Palace Ruins & Hazar Sutan Citadel
description: Towering over the urban village of Begumpur in the heart of Jahanpanah (the fourth historic city of Delhi), Bijay Mandal ('Victory Pavilion') is an enigmatic 14th-century multi-tiered palace complex constructed by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq around 1325 CE, featuring an elevated stone observation tower commanding 360-degree vistas across southern Delhi, underground treasure vaults with stone trap-doors, and the archaeological foundations of the famed 'Hazar Sutan' (Palace of a Thousand Pillars) visited and documented by Moroccan explorer Ibn Battuta.

name: Chor Minar (Tower of Severed Heads)
description: Standing majestically within a landscaped traffic island park in Hauz Khas Enclave, constructed around 1300 CE under the reign of Sultan Alauddin Khalji of the Delhi Sultanate, Chor Minar ('Tower of Thieves') is a circular rubble stone tower set upon a square masonry platform, studded with precisely 225 circular recesses or arrow-slits through which wooden spikes were thrust to display the severed heads of executed thieves, bandits, and rebel Mongol generals as a terrifying deterrent against crime and treason.

name: Dargah Hazrat Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki Mehrauli
description: Situated deep inside the historic labyrinthine lanes of Mehrauli village near Gandhak Ki Baoli, this revered 13th-century Sufi sanctuary is the oldest dargah in Delhi, enshrining Hazrat Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (1173-1235 CE), the primary disciple and spiritual successor of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer, so venerated that Sultan Iltutmish named the Qutub Minar in his honor and successive Mughal emperors sought burial within its sacred precincts, serving as the spiritual culmination of the annual secular festival 'Phool Walon Ki Sair'.

name: Dilli Haat INA (Crafts & Pan-India Food Bazaar)
description: Situated on Sri Aurobindo Marg opposite INA Market, established in 1994 by Delhi Tourism and the Ministry of Textiles, Dilli Haat INA is India's most beloved open-air crafts bazaar and gastronomic cultural village, designed with traditional thatched-roof brick stalls that rotate every 15 days to allow master rural artisans, national award winners, and weavers from every corner of India to sell authentic handloom shawls, Madhubani paintings, brassware, and woodwork directly to buyers, alongside 25 authentic state-run food stalls serving delicacies from Kashmir to Kerala.

name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Central Park
description: A public community recreation and green park honoring Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, equipped with jogging trails, open gym facilities, and lush lawns for community fitness and leisure.

name: Firoz Shah Tughlaq Madrasa & Assembly Hall
description: Stretching in an expansive L-shaped configuration along the eastern and southern edges of the Hauz Khas reservoir, established in 1352 CE by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq, this was the most prestigious center of higher learning in the medieval Islamic world, comprising two-storey colonnaded dalans (classrooms and student hostels), tiered arcades, assembly halls, jharokha balconies projecting toward the water, and small domed chhatris where students studied theology, astronomy, and mathematics.

name: Gandhak Ki Baoli (Sultanate Sulphur Stepwell Mehrauli)
description: Situated near the southern edge of Mehrauli village adjacent to Dargah Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki, built between 1210 and 1236 CE by Sultan Shams-ud-din Iltutmish, Gandhak Ki Baoli is celebrated as the oldest surviving stepwell in Delhi, named after the distinctive sulfurous scent ('gandhak') of its therapeutic subterranean waters, featuring five descending tiers of sandstone pillars, broad stepped terraces, and natural spring water historically credited with healing dermatological ailments.

name: Garden of Five Senses
description: A public sensory theme park spread over 20 acres developed by Delhi Tourism, designed to stimulate all five senses with aroma gardens, bamboo groves, gushing water streams, solar parks, and rock sculptures.

name: Green Park & Deer Park
description: A sprawling nature sanctuary also known as A.N. Jha Deer Park, home to spotted deer enclosures, hundreds of free-roaming peacocks, a duck pond, and scattered Lodi-era stone monuments (Bagh-i-Alam Gumbad).

name: Hauz Khas Fort and Lake
description: Originally excavated by Alauddin Khalji in 1296 as Hauz-i-Alai to supply water to Siri Fort, expanded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq who built a world-renowned madrasa, assembly halls, and his own lakeside stone tomb.

name: Jahanpanah City Forest Chirag Delhi
description: Spanning 435 acres in South Delhi bordered by Greater Kailash II, Chirag Delhi, and Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah City Forest is one of Delhi's most cherished urban natural reserves, densely forested with mature neem, jamun, and amaltas trees, featuring a winding 7-kilometer asphalt and earthen fitness track, open-air calisthenics gyms, and serving as a peaceful sanctuary for hundreds of peacocks, parakeets, and nilgai antelopes.

name: Jahaz Mahal & Hauz-i-Shamsi Mehrauli
description: Perched on the northeastern embankment of the sacred 1229 CE Hauz-i-Shamsi reservoir in Mehrauli, constructed during the Lodi period (c. 1452-1526 CE), Jahaz Mahal ('Ship Palace') owes its romantic name to its visual reflection in the lake water that gave it the appearance of an anchored ship, featuring intricate red sandstone chhatri domes, blue glazed ceramic tile inlays, arched courtyards, and serving as the historic focal point for Delhi's beloved annual flower festival 'Phool Walon Ki Sair'.

name: Jamali Kamali Mosque & Tomb Mehrauli
description: Situated within the tranquil 200-acre Mehrauli Archaeological Park, built between 1528 and 1535 CE during the transition from the Lodi dynasty to Mughal rule, this celebrated architectural complex comprises a grand red sandstone mosque with five multi-cusped arched bays that served as the stylistic prototype for the famous Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque, and an adjacent flat-roofed tomb chamber whose interior is breathtakingly ornamented with cobalt-blue and yellow glazed tiles, painted ceilings, and Persian verses composed by the Sufi poet Shaikh Jamali.

name: Khirki Mosque (Four-Quadrant Latticed Mosque)
description: Situated in Khirki Village opposite Select Citywalk in Saket, constructed around 1375 CE by Khan-i-Jahan Junan Shah (the famous Prime Minister of Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq), Khirki Mosque ('Mosque of Windows') is one of the most unusual mosques in Islamic architectural history: unlike conventional open-courtyard mosques, it is entirely roofed over except for four symmetric open courtyards, crowned by 85 stone domes and enclosed by heavy fortress-like rubble walls pierced by exquisite perforated stone lattice windows ('khirkis').

name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
description: Spread over 200 contiguous acres adjoining Qutub Minar, an extraordinary open-air archaeological park preserving over 1,000 years of continuous occupation, containing over 100 historic monuments including Jamali Kamali Mosque and Rajon ki Baoli.

name: Moth Ki Masjid (Mosque from a Single Grain of Moth Seed)
description: Situated in Uday Park near South Extension, built in 1505 CE by Miyan Bhiya (Prime Minister of Sultan Sikandar Lodi), Moth Ki Masjid ('Mosque of the Moth Lentil') is renowned in Delhi folklore: according to legend, Sikandar Lodi playfully gave a single moth lentil seed to his minister, who planted it, harvested its multiplied yield across successive seasons, and used the enormous accumulated agricultural profits to fund this architectural masterpiece, featuring a five-bay arched facade, octagonal two-storey corner chhatris, red sandstone and white marble inlays, and plaster ceiling rosettes.

name: Mughal Jharna & Water Cascade Mehrauli
description: Located in a lush garden depression south of Hauz-i-Shamsi in Mehrauli, Jharna ('Waterfall') is a historic Mughal pleasure garden constructed around 1700 CE and expanded by Emperor Akbar Shah II in the early 19th century, designed with stone channels, stepped cascades, aqueducts, and baradari pavilions where cooling overflow waters from Hauz-i-Shamsi cascaded over sculpted stone chutes into lower pleasure pools where royal courtiers gathered during the monsoon festival of Sair-e-Gulfaroshan.

name: Munda Gumbad & Nili Mosque Hauz Khas
description: Standing on a raised island mound in the northwestern waters of Hauz Khas lake, Munda Gumbad is a massive, dome-less rubble stone pavilion built by Alauddin Khalji in the early 14th century as a water-palace pavilion to enjoy cooling breezes; while nearby in the village stands Nili Mosque (Neeli Masjid), built in 1505 CE during the reign of Sikandar Lodi by Kasumbhil, celebrated for its surviving frieze of radiant cobalt-blue glazed tiles decorating its entrance archway.

name: Qila Rai Pithora Fort Ramparts & Statues
description: Encompassing the conserved archaeological park and massive surviving ramparts along Press Enclave Road in Malviya Nagar, Qila Rai Pithora is celebrated as the first of the seven historic cities of Delhi, built in the late 12th century by the legendary Chahamana (Chauhan) Rajput ruler Prithviraj Chauhan by expanding the older 11th-century Lal Kot citadel, featuring massive rubble bastions, thick stone ramparts, a museum gallery, and a heroic colossal bronze equestrian statue of Prithviraj Chauhan.

name: Qutub Minar
description: Commenced in 1199 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish, a soaring 72.5-meter red sandstone victory minaret covered in intricate Quranic inscriptions and fluted stone balconies.

name: Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque & Iron Pillar of Delhi
description: Forming the archaeological nucleus of the UNESCO World Heritage Qutub Complex in Mehrauli, Quwwat-ul-Islam ('Might of Islam') Mosque was commenced in 1193 CE by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, constructed with carved stone colonnades and capitals salvaged from 27 ancient Hindu and Jain temples, centered around the world-famous 7.2-meter-tall Iron Pillar of Delhi, forged during the Gupta Empire in the 4th century CE under King Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, celebrated globally for its metallurgical mystery of remaining completely rust-free despite 1,600 years of exposure to tropical monsoons.

name: Rajon Ki Baoli (Mughal-Era Stepwell Mehrauli)
description: Hidden within the dense neem and keekar forest of Mehrauli Archaeological Park, built in 1506 CE by Daulat Khan during the reign of Sultan Sikandar Lodi for masons ('rajon'), this extraordinary four-tiered subterranean stepwell descends deep into the earth via broad stone steps, flanked on each level by multi-tiered recessed arcaded galleries, a decorated 12-pillared chhatri pavilion, and an adjacent Lodi-era stone mosque with blue tile inlays, praised as Delhi's most picturesque and architecturally complete historic stepwell.

name: Satpula Dam-Weir (Seven Bridges Sluice)
description: Straddling the former stream of the southern city wall of Jahanpanah near Khirki Village, constructed in 1343 CE by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Satpula ('Seven Bridges') is an extraordinary medieval hydraulic engineering marvel: a dual-level stone weir and fortified bridge featuring seven principal arched sluice openings fitted with grooved vertical slots for wooden sluice gates to regulate agricultural irrigation and defensive moat water levels, flanked at either end by octagonal fortified defense towers equipped with schools and guard barracks.

name: Shahpur Jat Historic Urban Village & Boutiques
description: Enclosed directly within the surviving perimeter walls of the 14th-century Siri Fort, Shahpur Jat is one of Delhi's most vibrant and eclectic urban villages, where ancient Sultanate stone arches, medieval granaries, and village chaupals blend seamlessly with chic indie designer fashion studios, bespoke bridal boutiques, artisanal coffee roasteries, hand-crafted leather workshops, and vibrant street art murals.

name: Shri Adya Katyayani Shaktipeeth Mandir (Chhatarpur Mandir)
description: Spanning 70 acres in South Delhi, a magnificent marble temple complex dedicated to Goddess Katyayani, constructed in 1974 by Baba Sant Nagpal featuring South and North Indian temple architecture.

name: Shrine of Hazrat Nasiruddin Mahmud Chirag-i-Dilli
description: Enclosed within the walled historical urban settlement of Chirag Delhi, this revered Sufi shrine complex is dedicated to Hazrat Nasiruddin Mahmud (1274-1356 CE), affectionately titled 'Chirag-i-Dilli' ('Lamp of Delhi') by his spiritual master Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya whom he succeeded as the fifth spiritual head of the Chishti Sufi order, featuring an open white marble courtyard, an ornate dome, peaceful prayer chambers, and surrounded by centuries-old gateway arches.

name: Siri Fort Citadel Walls & Archaeological Bastions
description: Constructed around 1303 CE by Sultan Alauddin Khalji, Siri was the second of the seven historical cities of Delhi, built as a massive military fortress city to protect the sultanate capital against catastrophic Mongol invasions, featuring colossal rubble masonry ramparts reinforced by circular bastions with flame-shaped battlements and arrow slits, where according to legend the severed heads ('sir') of 8,000 slain Mongol warriors were embedded directly into the foundation masonry, giving Siri its name.

name: Tibet House Museum Lodhi Road
description: Situated on Institutional Area along Lodhi Road, established in 1965 by His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama as the cultural embassy of Tibet in India, Tibet House Museum preserves and showcases the endangered cultural, religious, and artistic heritage of Tibet, housing an exquisite museum gallery displaying sacred 15th-to-19th-century silk thangka paintings, gilded bronze statues of Buddhist deities, ritual prayer instruments, ancient Tibetan xylograph manuscripts, and a specialized library on Buddhist philosophy.

name: Tilpath Valley Biodiversity Park Sainik Farm
description: Situated in the southern Aravalli ridge foothills near Sainik Farm, spanning 172 acres of rugged undulating terrain, Tilpath Valley Biodiversity Park is one of Delhi's newest and most scenic nature reserves, featuring restored native savannas, thorn scrub forests, stone check-dams recharging groundwater, and hiking trails winding through quiet quartzite valleys that shelter Indian rock pythons, porcupines, monitor lizards, and over 100 bird species.

name: Tomb of Bahlol Lodi & Lal Gumbad Chirag Delhi
description: Situated near the western entrance of Chirag Delhi, constructed in 1489 CE by his son Sikandar Lodi, this unique 12-pillared stone tomb enshrines Sultan Bahlol Lodi, founder of the Afghan Lodi dynasty that ruled North India from 1451 to 1526, featuring five low fluted domes and arched openings; while nearby stands Lal Gumbad ('Red Dome' or Rakabwala Gumbad), built in 1397 CE for Saint Kabiruddin Auliya, celebrated for its sloping red sandstone walls and white marble band inlays.

name: Tomb of Firoz Shah Tughlaq Hauz Khas
description: Standing at the prominent southern intersection where the two multi-tiered college wings of the Hauz Khas madrasa meet, constructed in 1388 CE, this square rubble masonry mausoleum of Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq is an architectural masterpiece of Tughlaq design, featuring battering stone walls, red sandstone and marble doorway bands, an exquisite plaster ceiling incised with colorful medallion carvings and Quranic calligraphy, and four stone cenotaphs overlooking the lake.

name: Tomb of Iltutmish & Alauddin Khalji's Madrasa
description: Situated in the northwest corner of the Qutub Complex, built in 1235 CE by Sultan Shams-ud-din Iltutmish for himself, this remarkable square sandstone tomb is celebrated for its open-to-the-sky cenotaph chamber whose interior walls are completely encrusted with lace-like Quranic calligraphy in Kufic and Naskh scripts and geometrical rosettes, featuring the earliest squinch arches built in India; while adjacent to the southwest lies Alauddin Khalji's L-shaped college (Madrasa) and his tomb, the first combined college-mausoleum in India.

name: Tomb of Muhammad Quli Khan & Metcalfe's Dilkusha
description: Perched on a high hillock overlooking the Qutub Minar within Mehrauli Archaeological Park, this unique architectural hybrid was originally built in the early 17th century as the octagonal tomb of Muhammad Quli Khan (brother of Adham Khan and foster brother of Emperor Akbar), until 1844 when Sir Thomas Metcalfe (the British Resident at the Mughal court) converted the tomb into his personal summer retreat named 'Dilkusha' ('Heart's Delight'), surrounding it with landscaped European terrace gardens, mock castellated guard houses, and picturesque ornamental follies.

name: Tughlaqabad Fort
description: Built in 1321 by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq, a titanic medieval stone fortress stretching over 6 kilometers with massive sloping stone ramparts up to 30 meters high, secret escape tunnels, and the fortified white-domed mausoleum.

name: Zafar Mahal & Moti Masjid Mehrauli
description: Nestled inside the crowded bazaar of Mehrauli near the Dargah of Bakhtiyar Kaki, Zafar Mahal represents the poignant final monument erected by the Mughal dynasty before its collapse: originally built by Emperor Akbar Shah II in the 1820s and extensively reconstructed in 1847 by Bahadur Shah Zafar II with the monumental three-storey red sandstone 'Hathi Gate' (Elephant Gate designed to allow royal elephants through), housing an open-air royal burial enclosure containing the empty grave plot ('Sardgah') prepared for Bahadur Shah Zafar, who tragically died and was buried in exile in Yangon, Myanmar.

name: Adilabad Fort & Citadel of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
description: Standing on a rocky quartzite ridge directly south of Tughlaqabad Fort across a former historic lake bed, constructed around 1327 CE by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Adilabad Fort (locally called Muhammadabad) is a formidable medieval fortress designed with sloping cyclopean stone walls, semi-circular bastions, fortified bailey gates, and high battlements conceived to augment the defensive perimeter of Tughlaqabad against invading Mongol forces.

name: Arab Ki Sarai & Grand Gateway Nizamuddin
description: Flanking the southwestern approach to Humayun's Tomb, built in the early 1560s by Queen Hamida Banu Begum (mother of Emperor Akbar), Arab Ki Sarai was a large walled residential caravanserai constructed to house the 300 Persian and Arab architects, stone carvers, and calligraphers brought from Iran to design and build Humayun's Tomb, entered through a colossal 14-meter-high arched gateway decorated with red sandstone, marble inlays, and blue-tiled panels, leading to an expansive marketplace and stone baoli.

name: Ashokan Rock Edict at Bahapur (East of Kailash)
description: Carved into a natural quartzite rock outcrop on a gentle hillock in a neighborhood park at Bahapur in East of Kailash, discovered in March 1966, this extraordinary epigraph is a Minor Rock Edict of Mauryan Emperor Ashoka the Great dating from approximately 250 BCE, containing ten lines of ancient Prakrit text inscribed in the Brahmi script exhorting citizens to practice Dharma, moral rectitude, and compassion toward all living beings, marking Delhi's oldest in-situ written historical artifact.

name: Badarpur Sarai Historic Three Gateways
description: Straddling the historic alignment of the Grand Trunk Road (Mathura Road) in Badarpur, constructed during the 17th century by Emperor Jahangir's court, Badarpur Sarai was a colossal fortified roadside caravanserai marking the historic southern customs entrance to Delhi, preserving its three monumental gateways (the Northern, Central, and Southern Gateways) crafted of red sandstone and quartzite with multi-cusped arches, upper guard chambers, battlements, and surviving enclosure walls.

name: Chausath Khamba (64-Pillared White Marble Pavilion)
description: Tucked deep inside the medieval lanes of Nizamuddin Basti near the Ghalib Academy, built in 1623-1624 CE by Mirza Aziz Koka (foster-brother of Emperor Akbar and governor of Gujarat) as a family mausoleum, Chausath Khamba ('Sixty-Four Pillars') is an architectural wonder crafted entirely from pure white Makrana marble, comprising a grand square pavilion whose roof is supported by precisely 64 monolithic carved marble pillars arranged in groups of four to create 25 internal bays, each crowned by a shallow hidden dome enclosed within exquisite pierced marble lattice jali screens.

name: Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya Dargah
description: The mausoleum of revered 14th-century Sufi saint Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya and poet Amir Khusrau, world-renowned for Thursday evening mystical Sufi Qawwali sessions that transport listeners into ecstasy.

name: Humayun's Tomb Delhi
description: Commissioned in 1558 by Empress Bega Begum and designed by Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, the first grand dynastic garden tomb of the Mughal Empire, acclaimed as the architectural prototype of the Taj Mahal.

name: Isa Khan Niyazi's Octagonal Tomb & Mosque Complex
description: Situated within the entrance forecourt of the UNESCO World Heritage Humayun's Tomb complex, constructed in 1547-1548 CE for the Afghan noble Isa Khan Niyazi (who served Sher Shah Suri), this breathtaking octagonal garden tomb predates Humayun's tomb by two decades, set within an exquisite sunken sunken octagonal garden enclosure, featuring triple-arched facades crowned by domed chhatris adorned with vibrant turquoise, yellow, and green glazed ceramic tiles, flanked by an ornate three-domed red sandstone mosque.

name: ISKCON Temple New Delhi (Glory of India Vedic Centre)
description: Inaugurated in 1998 by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on Hare Krishna Hill, featuring 90-foot temple spires, an automated animatronics museum, and the Astha Kunj landscaped public park.

name: Kalindi Kunj & Yamuna Riverfront Park
description: Situated on the banks of the Yamuna River near the Okhla Barrage on the Delhi-Noida border, Kalindi Kunj is a popular public park and riverfront promenade celebrated for its terraced green lawns, illuminated musical water fountains, amusement joyrides, and sunset viewpoints overlooking the Yamuna River and the Okhla Bird Sanctuary marshlands.

name: Kalkaji District Park & Lotus Pond
description: Occupying a scenic hillside directly adjacent to the Bahá'í Lotus Temple in South Delhi, Kalkaji District Park is a beautifully terraced municipal park featuring winding pathways, landscaped rock gardens, cascading streams, musical fountains, a lotus pond, and lush green knolls that offer stunning elevated viewpoint angles of the petals of the Lotus Temple rising against the sky.

name: Lotus Temple (Bahá'í House of Worship)
description: Dedicated in 1986, an architectural wonder shaped like a blossoming white lotus with 27 free-standing marble petals arranged in clusters of three, welcoming people of all religions to meditate in silence.

name: Mausoleum of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq & Causeway
description: Connected to the southern fortress walls of Tughlaqabad Fort by an ancient 228-meter arched stone causeway (which originally bridged a massive artificial reservoir), this striking 1325 CE pentagonal fortified mausoleum built by Sultan Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq for himself is hailed as an architectural masterpiece, featuring dramatically sloping red sandstone walls symbolizing martial strength, crowned by a pure white marble dome (one of the earliest marble domes in Delhi), battlements, and housing the tombs of Ghiyasuddin, his wife, and his son Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

name: Millennium Park (Indraprastha Park) Ring Road
description: Sprawling across 85 landscaped acres along Ring Road beside the Yamuna River near Sarai Kale Khan, opened in 2004 by the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Indraprastha Park (Millennium Park) is one of Delhi's largest riverside recreational spaces, renowned for the colossal, gleaming white World Peace Pagoda (Vishwa Shanti Stupa) inaugurated in 2007 by the Dalai Lama and President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, surrounded by formal rose gardens, water cascades, an amphitheatre, and rolling green knolls.

name: Nehru Place IT Market
description: Asia's biggest and most bustling commercial electronics and computer hardware hub, housing thousands of tech shops, component distributors, mobile service centers, and printeries.

name: Okhla Bird Sanctuary
description: A 4-square-kilometer wetland sanctuary on the Yamuna River where it enters Uttar Pradesh, home to over 300 bird species including thousands of migratory waterfowl traveling via the Central Asian Flyway.

name: Shri Kalkaji Mandir (Ancient Kali Temple of Delhi)
description: Perched on a rocky hillock on the Delhi Ridge near Nehru Place in South Delhi, Shri Kalkaji Mandir (Manokamna Siddha Peetha) is revered as one of the oldest surviving holy shrines in North India, dating according to Hindu tradition back 3,000 years to the Mahabharata period when Lord Krishna and the Pandavas worshipped Goddess Kali here before the Kurukshetra war, featuring an octagonal 18th-century marble-clad sanctum, brass bells, and intense devotional energy during Navratri.

name: Sunder Nursery Heritage Park
description: A 90-acre heritage city park created in the 16th century, meticulously restored by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture, housing six UNESCO World Heritage monuments, 300 tree species, formal Persian gardens, and lotus ponds.

name: Surviving Kos Minars of Delhi (Badarpur, Mathura Road & Kureni)
description: Dating from the 16th and 17th centuries when Sher Shah Suri and Mughal Emperors Akbar and Jahangir built the Grand Trunk Road network, Kos Minars ('Milestone Towers') were solid cylindrical and conical masonry towers erected at intervals of one 'kos' (approximately 3.6 km / 2.2 miles) with fresh horses, post riders, and caravan security; surviving examples across Delhi include the Badarpur Border Kos Minar, the Apollo Hospital Mathura Road Kos Minar, the Mahigirm Kos Minar, and the Kureni Village Kos Minar in Narela.

name: Tomb of Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana Nizamuddin
description: Standing in a verdant garden along Mathura Road in Nizamuddin, built in 1598 CE by the celebrated poet-general and Navratna of Emperor Akbar's court, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana (famous for his immortal Hindi dohas / couplets of 'Rahim') for his wife Mah Banu and where he was later buried in 1627, this monumental square mausoleum was the direct stylistic prototype for the Taj Mahal, featuring imposing red sandstone facades once covered in marble that was famously stripped in 1753 to build Safdarjung's Tomb, recently restored to magnificent glory by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture.

name: Waste to Wonder Theme Park
description: Inaugurated in 2019 near Sarai Kale Khan, an innovative 7-acre green theme park featuring monumental scaled replicas of the Seven Wonders of the World, constructed entirely using 150 tons of industrial and automobile scrap metal.

name: Air Force Museum Palam (Vintage Aircraft & War Memorial)
description: Located at the Indian Air Force Station Palam near Delhi Airport, the Air Force Museum is India's premier military aviation institution, preserving the heroic operational history of the Indian Air Force from its founding in 1932, featuring an indoor hangar display of historic aircraft (including the Supermarine Spitfire, Hawker Tempest, de Havilland Vampire, and Folland Gnat 'Sabre Slayer'), an outdoor apron showcasing colossal transport aircraft, radar units, surface-to-air missiles, and captured Pakistani military war trophies from the 1965 and 1971 wars.

name: Aravalli Biodiversity Park Vasant Kunj
description: Sprawling across 692 acres of restored scrubland and rocky quartzite terrain in Vasant Kunj, transformed from abandoned mining pits into a thriving ecological sanctuary by Delhi University ecologists and the DDA, the Aravalli Biodiversity Park recreates the primeval dry deciduous forests and native shrub communities of the ancient Aravalli range, supporting over 1,000 indigenous plant species, a specialized butterfly conservatory, 200 species of birds, and healthy populations of nilgai, golden jackals, porcupines, and civets.

name: Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF Climbing Wall Moti Bagh)
description: Situated on Benito Juarez Marg near South Campus in Moti Bagh, established in 1957, the Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) is the national apex body for mountaineering, trekking, and sport climbing in India, celebrated for housing an international-competition-standard 50-foot artificial sport climbing wall offering top-rope, lead, and speed climbing routes under certified instructors, alongside the Himalayan Museum documenting iconic Indian Everest expeditions and rare alpine literature.

name: Mehram Nagar Katra & Walled Caravanserai
description: Situated adjacent to Terminal 1 of Delhi Airport in Delhi Cantonment, established around 1639 CE by Mehram Khan (a trusted eunuch noble of Emperor Jahangir and supervisor of the royal harem under Shah Jahan), Mehram Nagar is an intact 17th-century walled village settlement entered via an imposing red sandstone arched gateway, featuring an ornate mosque, vaulted merchant shops, residential cells, and an enclosed pleasure garden.

name: Neela Hauz Biodiversity Park & Constructed Wetland
description: Nestled near the Aruna Asaf Ali Marg flyover adjacent to Sanjay Van in South Delhi, Neela Hauz ('Blue Lake') was an ancient natural freshwater lake that had degenerated into a severely polluted sewage pit until 2016, when DDA ecologists implemented an innovative, chemical-free constructed wetland biofilter system using specialized aquatic plants (typha, phragmites) and gravel beds to naturally purify millions of liters of raw sewage daily, reviving the lake into an idyllic sanctuary with crystal-clear water, blooming white lotus, and resident spot-billed ducks.

name: Sanjay Van South Delhi Forest Trails
description: Covering 783 acres of contiguous woodland on the Southern Ridge between Mehrauli and JNU, Sanjay Van is one of Delhi's most popular green lungs, densely blanketed in indigenous babool, dhau, and neem trees, crisscrossed by miles of stone-paved walking and cycling tracks, featuring 12th-century stone ramparts of Qila Rai Pithora, several ancient Sufi shrines (including Dargah of Hazrat Ashiq Allah), and serving as a haven for over 150 species of birds, nilgai antelopes, and golden jackals.

name: Sulabh International Museum of Toilets Mahavir Enclave
description: Situated at the Sulabh International complex on Palam-Dabri Road in Mahavir Enclave near Dwarka, established in 1992 by the renowned social reformer and sanitation pioneer Dr. Bindeshwar Pathak, this unique and witty museum is ranked by Time magazine among the world's top 10 weirdest and most fascinating museums, tracing the 4,500-year evolution of sanitation technology from the brick-lined sewers of Mohenjo-daro to medieval European chamber pots, Victorian floral porcelain commodes, and space-age zero-gravity astronaut toilets.

name: Vasant Vihar Park
description: A tranquil, leafy green park nestled within the diplomatic and residential precinct of Vasant Vihar, featuring manicured flowerbeds, mature neem and amaltas canopies, and quiet jogging pathways.

name: Bharat Darshan Park Punjabi Bagh
description: Sprawling across 8.5 acres along Ring Road in Punjabi Bagh, opened in December 2021 by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), Bharat Darshan Park is an innovative eco-friendly theme park showcasing detailed miniature replicas of 21 famous Indian historical monuments—including the Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, Konark Sun Temple, Hampi chariot, Victoria Memorial, and Meenakshi Temple—constructed entirely out of 350 metric tons of discarded scrap metal, junk automobile parts, and old iron rods, illuminated beautifully by energy-efficient solar lights.

name: Hashtsal Minar (Shah Jahan's Hunting Minaret 1634)
description: Standing amid the narrow village lanes of Hashtsal Village near Uttam Nagar in West Delhi, constructed in 1634 CE by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, Hashtsal Minar ('Tower of Eight Jackals' or 'Elephant Palace Tower') is a 17-meter (55-foot) tall red sandstone and brick minaret resembling a miniature Qutub Minar, featuring three tapering storeys with circular and angular flutings, an internal spiral staircase, and an octagonal plinth, built as an elevated shooting tower for Shah Jahan during royal elephant and nilgai hunting expeditions.

name: Rajouri Garden Delhi
description: One of West Delhi's most popular commercial districts, celebrated for upscale wedding apparel boutiques, multi-storey shopping complexes, and mouthwatering street food (chole bhature, chaat, kulfi).

name: Tagore Garden Delhi
description: A well-planned western Delhi residential locality featuring manicured neighborhood parks, community walking tracks, and proximity to the vibrant Pacific Mall entertainment complex.
